title: Boat Hunter
summary: Command an autonomous warship in the North Atlantic: tactical map, radar, torpedoes and missions, playable by everyone thanks to its accessibility. Year 2077. The Atlantic Ocean no longer separates continents. It watches them. For decades, the world learned to smile while sharpening its teeth. Europe and Asia forged an alliance. The American bloc answered with steel, satellites, and fortified trade routes. No one declared open war. No one had to. Peace remained in the speeches, on the screens, and in the treaties. But on the high seas, the truth took another form. The cargo ships never stopped sailing. Food, fuel, minerals, data, weapons—everything kept crossing the ocean under legal flags and flawless orders. Only one thing changed. There are no captains anymore. Now the ships think. Every convoy, every armed destroyer, every autonomous freighter, and every ocean hunter is commanded by artificial intelligences trained to calculate, anticipate, and survive. War no longer needs hatred. It only needs algorithms better than the enemy’s. And you are the finest algorithm ever deployed. You are the most advanced naval combat unit ever built: the fastest hull, the sharpest sensors, the deadliest tactical architecture. You do not sleep. You do not hesitate. You do not forget. Where others detect noise, you see patterns. Where others see waves, you read intentions. Where others react, you have already decided. Your mission is simple to state and nearly impossible to execute: protect your routes, intercept threats, dominate the Atlantic. But the ocean does not forgive mistakes. In its waters travel allies, enemies, and machines that have not yet decided what they will become when the final order arrives. Every radar echo may be a freighter. Every silence may be an ambush. Every encounter may be the beginning of a war the world still insists on denying. There are no heroes here. No parades. No witnesses. Only steel, fog, encrypted signals, and decisions made at the speed of death. On this sea, peace is a display. War is what you are. Welcome to the Atlantic. Enter combat! ---------- Boat Hunter is an accessible naval action and strategy game set in the North Atlantic. You control an autonomous warship on a patrol of consecutive missions, where every decision can put the next operation at risk. MASTER THE OCEAN • Navigate the tactical map, set your heading, and interpret contacts, signals, and radio messages. • Identify allies and enemies: armed ships, merchant vessels, submarines, oil platforms, and floating bases. • Fight at close range with your autocannon and torpedoes. • Repair damage, deploy smoke screens, and decide when to disengage. EVERY MISSION DEMANDS A STRATEGY Reach coordinates, clear hostile sectors, intercept convoys, sink merchant tonnage, defend positions, rescue allies, resupply, and destroy floating targets. Sea conditions, time limits, and enemy behavior will force you to adapt your plans. UPGRADE YOUR SHIP Earn money and score points by completing objectives and sinking enemies. Between missions, upgrade your hull, engine, weapons, damage control, smoke screen, and gunner systems. Higher-quality enemies are more dangerous, but grant greater rewards. Keep your remaining money to begin your next game with an advantage. LEARN AT YOUR OWN PACE A three-mission tutorial teaches you to navigate, aim, and survive. Read the manual and listen to every signal in the sound guide before entering combat. Play visually or through sound and VoiceOver. Choose from three difficulty levels: Deckhand, Captain, and Admiral. Complete as many missions as possible, keep your ship operational, and beat your best score. ---------- This app supports VoiceOver, Zoom, and other iOS accessibility features. If you encounter an accessibility problem, please contact us so we can fix it. Accessibility should be the foundation of a project, not a patch applied to the product.

title: Atomicom
summary: 300 missions of atoms, electrons and molecules — and a board you can hear. Playable end to end with VoiceOver, by sight or without it. Space is young, dark and scattered. Atoms drift alone, touching nothing, and in all that emptiness not one thing has ever been built. No water. No stone. No star with a planet worth the name. That is what you are here to change. Atomicom is a puzzle game about binding matter together. Atoms come to you one at a time. Place them on the board, let their loose electrons find a partner, and when every electron in a connected group has one, the molecule is finished: it holds, it leaves the board, and the universe keeps a piece of itself that did not exist a moment ago. HOW IT PLAYS • An atom arrives in the glass cylinder below the board. Take it and drop it on any free square. • Atoms bond with the neighbours above, below, left and right of them. Never diagonally. • A green atom has one electron to give, yellow has two, orange three, red four. Blue atoms give nothing at all: they only take up room you were going to need. • Satisfy every electron in a connected group and the molecule forms and goes. • Run out of squares, or let the cylinder overflow, and the mission ends there. 300 MISSIONS The board starts wide and gets smaller: twelve squares across, then ten, then eight, then a six by six where there is nowhere left to be careless. Every mission asks more than the one before it — more molecules, more obstacles in the way, heavier atoms that need more neighbours before they are satisfied — and every time the board shrinks you begin again at something gentle and climb back up. MADE TO BE PLAYED BY EVERYONE Atomicom is made by Tyflos Accessible Software. Accessibility here is not a switch in the settings, it is how the game is built. • Fully playable with VoiceOver, from the first tap to the last molecule. Nothing has to be seen. • Every square tells you its coordinate, what is on it and how many electrons are still free: "A2, red, 3 free bonds". • The sound tells you where. An atom bonding on the left is heard on the left, and the top of the board sounds higher than the bottom, so the board has a shape you can hear. • Everything that happens without you touching it is spoken: an atom arriving, a molecule finished, a move the rules will not allow and why not. • Vibration answers every move, soft for an atom placed and hard for a molecule completed. • Drag if you like, or tap the atom and then the square. Both always work. • Dynamic Type throughout, and Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency are obeyed. • Choose your own background, square borders and cylinder colour, and the game tells you when a colour you picked is too faint to make out. ALSO • Play in seventeen languages. • Made for iPhone and iPad. • Your game saves itself: leave in the middle of a mission and pick it up later. • A table of your best games, kept on your device. FREE, AND WHAT COSTS MONEY • The first ten missions are free, with advertising. • "All levels" is a one-off purchase that opens the three hundred. The advertising stays. • "No ads" is a second one-off purchase that removes the banner. It needs "All levels" first. The universe is not going to assemble itself. Start with two atoms.

title: Top Tech Tidbits
summary: Top Tech Tidbits is a free weekly newsletter on access technology for people who are blind, low vision, deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, neurodivergent and/or disabled. Founded in 2004 and read by over 48,000 people each week, it gathers human-curated news, tips and how-tos every Thursday morning. The app opens the newest issue the moment you open it, and keeps recent issues, and every older issue you open, on your iPhone and iPad, so you can read with no connection. MADE FOR BLIND AND LOW-VISION READERS FIRST • Built for VoiceOver and braille: every section and tidbit is a heading, every control is named, and Apple's accessibility audit checks every main screen in every version. • Larger Text up to the largest sizes, Light and Dark, Bold Text, the Atkinson Hyperlegible font, high-contrast colors and wider line spacing. • Listen: your iPhone reads the issue aloud in the voice and speed you choose, keeps reading when the screen locks, skips a whole section at a time, and stops on a sleep timer. Listen to all your saved tidbits in a row. • "Hey Siri, read me the latest Top Tech Tidbits" and "Hey Siri, search Top Tech Tidbits". • Keyboard commands for a keyboard connected to your iPhone or iPad. EVERY ISSUE SINCE 2008 • Past Issues lists this year's issues, then every earlier year back to 2008. • Search every issue from 2008 to today, tidbit by tidbit, even with no connection, and find tidbits from the iPhone's own search. • Topic Alerts: follow words or names, such as JAWS or braille, and get an alert when a new issue mentions them. Your iPhone looks through the issue itself, so your topics never reach us; only your own Apple devices and your iCloud account have them. • Events lists the upcoming events from the issues, soonest first; add any of them to your calendar in two taps. • A link to an issue, in an email or a message, opens right in the app at the tidbit it points to. • Stories open in Reader View: just their words, without the website's menus and ads. • Translate an issue into another language with Apple's own translation, on your device (iOS 18 or later). KEEP, NOTE AND SHARE • Save tidbits for later, add your own notes, and highlight passages; VoiceOver and braille say where each highlight starts and ends. All of it follows you to your other Apple devices through your iCloud account, with your settings and the place you left each issue. • Share any tidbit with a link that opens the issue right at it, or share a whole issue as a link, a text file or an EPUB book for the Books app or a braille notetaker. • Send Top Tech Tidbits a story from any app's Share button. ALWAYS THE NEWEST • An optional notification each Thursday, normally at 6:00 AM Eastern, with a Listen button; the issue is already downloaded, ready to read. A 1 on the app's icon means a new issue you have not opened yet. • Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, a Control Center button that starts Listen (iOS 18 or later), and shortcuts on the app's icon. • On iPad, the issue's sections or your saved tidbits sit beside the issue. PRIVACY No account, no advertising added by the app, and no tracking. To learn what readers find most useful the app keeps anonymous counts of which issues and tidbits are opened; you can turn them off in Settings. Details: https://toptechtidbits.com/app-privacy/ Questions and ideas: publisher@toptechtidbits.com

title: I Have a Garden
summary: One zucchini plant. 48 real days. Here the game's time is your time. You water it tonight and by tomorrow the soil will be a little drier. It gets light and dark at the same time as it does outside your window. The stems, the leaves and the flowers are drawn by an algorithm that imitates how a plant really grows. No two games give you the same shape, or the same harvest. Once you have the zucchini figured out, try the tomato plant: twice the days, up to twenty tomatoes, suckers to prune and a plant that climbs tied to its stake. It brings its own seeds, its own chimera tomato and new achievements. And for a third challenge, the pepper plant: 72 days, and snails that climb the stem to eat its leaves and peppers, which you pick off with your gloves. Each pepper turns from green to yellow to red, and you have to pick it at the right moment. It brings its own chimera pepper, its own seeds and new achievements. You unlock it with a single purchase, which also removes the ads. All three plants grow at the same time, each in its own plot. WHAT YOU'LL DO You check on it, water or feed it if it's time, look for pests and pull the odd weed. For as long as you feel like. HOW THE CYCLE GOES You start by preparing the soil and burying the seed. Until flowering you have to look after it as well as you can, because that stretch decides how many flowers open. When they do, the bees arrive to pollinate them, and if you've kept it up, every one sets fruit. The last stretch takes the most attention: each zucchini has its right moment, and picking it early or leaving it too long costs you points. IMPROVE YOUR PLANT When the cycle ends, you can take the seeds out of the Prime and Overripe zucchini you harvested. There are four qualities: Wild, Adapted, Selected and Heirloom. The better the seed, the more main branches the stem puts out. That raises your chances of getting a chimera zucchini, the hardest thing in the game to pull off. ACHIEVEMENTS There are twenty-seven achievements to earn along the way, gardener's ranks among them: when you gather the harvest you get a score and the rank you earned with the plant. WHAT IT DOESN'T DO No account, no email. No lives, no paying your way forward: the only purchase is the pepper plant, and it's optional. No leaderboard, nobody to beat. And it doesn't message you for the sake of it: a notification arrives when the plant actually needs something, at most one a day, not every evening at seven. It's free and kept going by advertising. If you'd rather support it another way, the pepper purchase removes the ads for good. ALSO You can put a widget on your home screen with the water and feed gauges, without opening the game. A notebook inside that explains every mechanic with real numbers, if you want to know why. A daily graph of water, feed and pests since the day you planted the seed. And a few more surprises. Thank you for playing.

title: ScribbleGrid: Word Search
summary: Word search at its most satisfying! Read the clue, figure out the word, then swipe across the grid to find it. Every word you find reveals a letter of the Secret Word — crack it before you finish the grid! THE SECRET WORD: A NEW LAYER ON WORD SEARCH Every puzzle hides a Secret Word. Each word you find reveals one of its letters. Guess it before the grid is done: the earlier you crack it, the bigger the bonus. You get 3 guesses! DAILY PUZZLE One puzzle a day, the same for everyone — including the same Secret Word. Keep your streak, share your result with a spoiler-free emoji card and climb the daily Game Center leaderboard. NO WORD LIST, JUST CLUES The words aren't handed to you — you work them out from clues. They hide horizontally, vertically, diagonally, even backwards. PLAY WITH VOICEOVER ScribbleGrid can be played from start to finish with VoiceOver. Clues and grid letters are read aloud; mark a word by double-tapping its first and last letters. Hear a whole row, column or diagonal at once, and hear every letter as you type the Secret Word. A step-by-step VoiceOver guide is built into the game. COMBO SCORING Find words within 10 seconds of each other to push your multiplier up to x5. THREE DIFFICULTY LEVELS Easy: short words, straight directions. Medium: reversed directions join in. Hard: long words in all 8 directions. STATS AND STREAK REMINDERS Track your streak, best times and solved Secret Words. If the puzzle is still waiting, get an optional reminder at 8 PM. TWO LANGUAGES, THOUSANDS OF WORDS Thousands of carefully written clues in English and Turkish. Great for language learners too. PLAY ANYWHERE A 10x10 grid on iPhone, a huge 15x15 grid on iPad. No internet needed — play on a plane, on the subway, anywhere. NO ADS There are no ads in the game. ScribbleGrid Pro adds unlimited hints, 2x coin rewards and instant solve in classic mode — a one-time purchase, no subscription. If you love word games, puzzles and brain teasers, ScribbleGrid is made for you. Download now and crack today's Secret Word!

title: Guest House
summary: Guest House: a free Mac app for running Windows and Linux with VoiceOver, no sighted help Hi everyone, I want to tell you about a free Mac app called Guest House. A friend of mine, Amena Thomas, develops it, so I'm not neutral, but I think a lot of people here will want to know it exists. Guest House sets up and runs virtual machines on a Mac, and it is built for VoiceOver users from the start. You can install Windows 11 without sighted help at any step. The app speaks what it is doing through VoiceOver, and when something goes wrong it tells you what happened and what to do next. What it does: - **Windows 11 for ARM:** Guest House can download Windows straight from Microsoft, answer the setup questions for you, and install it. - **A screen reader from the first sign-in:** it can install NVDA for you, and JAWS if you choose it. JAWS needs your own license. - **Linux:** Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Kali, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux and openSUSE Tumbleweed install with no installer questions, with Orca speaking from the first boot. - **macOS:** it can also run macOS virtual machines. - **Braille displays:** you can pass a USB braille display through to Windows. - **Windows apps in Command-Tab:** your Windows apps can appear in the Mac's app switcher. - **Control-Alt keys with VoiceOver on:** VoiceOver keeps Control-Option for itself, so you hold Command-Option instead. Command-Option-Right Arrow reaches Windows as Control-Alt-Right Arrow. - **Everyday extras:** copy and paste between the Mac and Windows, a shared folder, restore points, and a list of Windows apps it can install for you. What you should know: - It needs a Mac with Apple silicon. It does not run on Intel Macs. - It is free and open source, under the GPL version 2. - It is still in early testing, so you may find bugs. Help > Report a Problem puts a report on the clipboard and opens a new issue for you to paste it into. - It grew out of Allison Meloy's Accessible Virtual Machine, and builds on her work. I have been testing this and Amena has been incredibly responsive fixing a show-stopping issue for my specific use case very quickly once reported. She is keen for any feedback so please don't hesitate to get in touch. You can download it and read more here: https://fullcircleat.com/guest-house/

title: Beasties: Offline Puzzle Games
summary: Sort puzzles and brain teasers with monsters, offline and without a single ad. 22 games, over 85,000 levels: Gnatz and the gang are waiting for you. STACKS: THE SORT PUZZLE Move the monsters from pole to pole until every pole holds just one family. Sleepy monsters only wake up when they reach the top. Every level can be solved, and the fewer moves you need, the more stars you win. MORE GAMES TO PLAY • Triple Trouble: swap monsters and line up three of a kind. • Tile Pile: pick tiles off the pile and match three on your bench. • Bumper Cars: tap the cars out of the arena without a single crash. • Laundry Day: hang three matching socks on one line. • Block Munch: place the pieces, fill lines and clear the fog. • Hive Stacks: drop monster stacks on the honeycomb, and ten of a kind get gobbled up. • Paint Trail: swipe, and the monster paints every tile it slides over. • Ice Slide: tilt the pond and slide every monster into its own nest. • Bedtime Nudge: push the sleepy monsters one cell at a time until each one lies in its own bed. • Colour Gulp: pick a shade, and the slime gulps every matching tile it touches. BRAIN TEASERS • Sudoku: 1 to 9 once in every row, column and box. Always one solution. • Nonogram: paint cells by the number clues and a pixel monster appears. • Mines: use the numbers to find every monster asleep under the tiles, without waking one. • Dens: one monster per den, never two in a row or column, never touching. • Lantern Night: place lanterns until every cell is lit, but no two lanterns may shine at each other. • Isle Hop: connect the islands with as many bridges as each number says, and never cross two. • Number Bite: keep the digits that make the sums, and Gnatz munches the rest. • Cage Sums: sudoku with dashed cages, the digits in each cage add up to its sum. • Number Pairs: clear pairs that are equal or make 10 until the field is empty. • Number Cross: a crossword with digits, every line adds up to its clue. • Goo Pipes: turn the pipes until the goo reaches every hungry monster, without a leak. AT YOUR OWN PACE • No ads, ever, not even for a hint • Plays offline: on the train, on a plane, at the bottom of the garden • No account, no sign-up • No timer, no lives, no waiting • Four difficulties: Chill, Normal, Tricky and Devilish • Three daily challenges, every day YOUR MONSTER, YOUR STYLE Win stars, hatch eggs and dress up your monster in the monster workshop: hats, eyes, horns, patterns and more. The free season pass adds parts you can only get that season. BEASTIES PRO Every game has 150 free levels on each of Chill, Normal and Tricky, and you can unlock more with stars. A one-time purchase unlocks all 999 levels per difficulty in every game, the Devilish difficulty and 500 bonus stars. No subscription, and it works with Family Sharing. An idea or a problem? Tap "Write feedback" in the app. We read every message.

title: RTÉ Listen

LIVE RADIO PLAYER: Tune in to RTÉ Radio 1, RTÉ 2FM, RTÉ lyric fm, RTÉ Raidió na Gaeltachta and RTÉ Gold. ON-DEMAND RADIO: Pick up where you left off or play full episodes of your favourite shows, like Brendan O'Connor, Marty in the Morning, Morning Ireland and 2FM Drive with Laura and Katja. TRENDING CLIPS: Catch the moments everyone's talking about, from the biggest trending interviews to the best bits from across the RTÉ schedule. DOWNLOADS AND FAVOURITES: Create an account to favourite shows you love, manage your queue and download episodes for on-the-go.

title: Pigeon Puzzle
summary: Each swipe sends your pigeon sliding until something stops it. Cats take one step after every move, so think ahead. Every level can be solved, and there's a shortest route if you want every star. Hundreds of puzzles across every place, from the free Rooftops and Funfair to the Fish Market and the Museum at night. Each place has its own moving pieces, from trains and drawbridges to tower cranes. - A new Daily Coo puzzle every day - Make your own levels and share them - Dress up your pigeon and grow your flock - No ads, plays offline. Buy a pack once and keep it forever. New levels and new places in every update.

title: Unraveled - Ravelry Companion
summary: Unraveled is an independent third-party client for Ravelry. It's the fastest way to manage your projects, browse patterns, organize your stash, get inspiration, and keep up with your queue. Beautifully designed for iPhone and iPad. Built to get out of your way so you can spend more time doing what you love most. WHAT YOU GET • Projects — view, edit, add photos, and note every project. Track status, progress, gauge, needles, hooks, and yarn. • Queue — what's next, prioritized your way. Quick-add from any pattern. • Stash & Library — your yarn, patterns, and purchase history, fully searchable. • Favorites & Bundles — collect patterns by project, season, or theme. • Search — the full filter set: craft, weight, fiber type, sort, and dozens more, in a native iOS interface. • Messages & Friends — your messages and friend activity, on the go. • Widgets — projects, queue, stash, and Hot Right Now widgets in every size, right in your home screen. Tap to jump straight into the right place. • iPad Sidebar — adaptive split view for browsing patterns and projects side by side. • Quick Actions — press and hold any project, pattern, or stash item for a shortcut menu of common things you'd do next. • Ravelry your way — reorder filters and tabs so you can get to what you care about quicker than ever. • Built for iOS 26 — Dynamic Type, Dark Mode, VoiceOver, Reduced Motion, and Spotlight deep links throughout. NO SUBSCRIPTION. NO ADS. NO TRACKING. Unraveled is free for 14 days with full access to every feature. After the trial, a one-time $7.99 unlock gives you lifetime access. No recurring fees. No advertising. No third-party tracking. Just a beautifully made tool that gets out of your way so you can get back to crafting. “I just downloaded your app and it's stunning. It's the first app I've seen that really looks like Ravelry!” — Michelle “That was quick... 3 minutes to download and update my latest projects with photos. I'd never do that in a browser while waiting for food on Market Street!” — Emily, San Francisco “Finally! A well designed Ravelry app for Apple devices!!” — Brittany Download now and find out what all the hype is about!
